liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Easy Wind** (3 reviews): The organ is heavy on this one, probably near the end of TC's time with the band; An early version of the song, with Jerry standing out [5][6][15]
- **Turn on Your Lovelight** (3 reviews): This Lovelight runs just under 31 minutes; Reviewer singles out Lovelight as especially great [9][14][16]
- **New Orleans** (2 reviews): The New Orleans into Searchin' into Good Lovin' sequence is rare and very fun; Raucous version of New Orleans [6][16]
- **Good Lovin'** (2 reviews): Jerry sings lead, with Pigpen and Bobby on backing vocals; Odd intro: the band starts two songs at once until Jerry plays the opening in unison with the drummers [7][8]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): A funky opener [16]
- **High Time** (1 review): Organ has nice vibrato, and the vocals build dynamically from a whisper to a strong finish [15]
- **Dire Wolf** (1 review): Jerry's voice sounds somewhat forced on Dire Wolf [15]
- **King Bee** (1 review): Pigpen is on fire during King Bee [6]

## Setlist highlights

- **New Orleans**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [17]
- **Searchin'**: earliest performance in the archive; rare: 5 archived performances [17]

## The recordings

- **gd69-08-29.sbd.cotsman.8996.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 10 songs; 80 min; rated 3.78/5 by 9 [1]. Said about its sound: Reviewer calls the incomplete show pretty good sounding when streamed; Reviewer finds the sound really good for a recording almost 40 years old; High-quality stereo audio with an excellent mix for 1969 [5][8][9]
- **gd1969-08-29.sbd.lai.9179.sbefail.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 79 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [3]
- **gd1969-08-29.123101.sbd-fixed.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 81 min; rated 3.5/5 by 4 [2]
- **gd1969-08-29.123075.sbd.miller.flac16**: soundboard; 10 songs; 81 min; rated 2.5/5 by 2 [4]

## Around the show

- Pigpen sings four songs: Easy Wind, Searchin', King Bee and Turn On Your Love Light [9]
- Casey Jones and Easy Wind here are earlier versions, as the band moves toward its Workingman's Dead sound [5]
- Early Good Lovin' with a straight-ahead, hard-driving rhythm; Phil and the drummers are strong [7]
- Reviewer rates this show as much better than the band's Woodstock performance [11]
- Leans more toward R&B than most Dead shows, despite having only ten songs [11]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd69-08-29.sbd.cotsman.8996.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Jeff Cook and JCotsman; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: A splice occurs about ninety seconds into Good Lovin'; The recording was normalized and retracked with Sound Forge and CDWave [1]
- **gd1969-08-29.sbd.lai.9179.sbefail.shnf**: taped by Wayne Gucwa; transferred by Mike Lai; source: Sdb>>?>>Dat>>CD [3]
- **gd1969-08-29.123101.sbd-fixed.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat [2]
- **gd1969-08-29.123075.sbd.miller.flac16**: transferred by Charlie Miller; source: SBD -> Master Reel -> Cassette -> Dat [4]
